steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Lightly grease a 10-inch pie plate. Combine lemon juice, sugar, eggs, coconut, flour, and milk in a large bowl. Stir until well blended and pour mixture into pie dish.
Bake in the preheated oven until center is set but slightly jiggly, about 35 minutes. Let pie cool completely before slicing.

raw_recipe.headline: Lemon Impossible Pie
raw_recipe.description: This tangy lemon impossible pie is made with fresh lemon juice, eggs, sugar, milk and coconut for an easy baked dessert.
raw_recipe.name: Lemon Impossible Pie

recipeInstructions.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).

review.reviewBody: Absolutely delicious! How? Double the lemon juice, add 2 tsp. lemon zest/rind and increase flour to 3/4 cup Everyone loved it!

Something’s screwed up with the quantity of milk in this recipe. It says 1.6599999666214 cup, so I just took a guess and added 1 cup milk. I’ve made a number of different impossible pies over the years, so I have a pretty good idea of what the consistency should be. This did not have the right consistency using 1 cup of milk. If I make this again, I’ll give 1-1/4 cups milk a try and bake for another 5 minutes. The beauty of these impossible pies is how quick and simple they are to prepare with minimal cleanup. This does taste very lemony, just needs some tweaking.

This was really good! I made a few changes. It looks pretty anemic but was delish! I used 1/2 cup lemon juice, cut the milk to 1 cup and only 3 eggs. Used a little extra flour and added lemon zest. We topped
Great recipe! I will make this again and try more lemon as well as making this in an actual crust.
I was skeptical at first but it really turn out beautifully.

I made this with 3/4 cup of flour, 2/3 cup lemon juice, and 1tps of lemon zest...The lemon strength is perfect, but it turned out more like a cake rather than a custard pie. I should probably lower the flour content back to 1/2 cup as the original recipe states.

I made this from another recipe. The only difference this recipe did not have is a tsp. vanilla. I would definitely use a tsp if not 1-1/2 tsp. It is like a custard filling and rather "blah"....needs the juice and zest from a whole lemon...not just a 1/3. I was thinking that perhaps it needs some pineapple juice (less some of the milk)...would make it again with those adjustments.

I liked it. I tried what the author suggested and used lime juice. I also decided to double the juice amount which tasted very good. I would suggest that you reduce the amount of liquid by the amount of increased fruit juice. I also decided to take a chance and substituted water for the milk since a scratch lemon or lime cooked pie filling use s water when its cooked. coconut/lime sounded good to me and the flavors were great. The only thing I didn't anticipate was the coconut floating to the top as it baked. But that wasn't a problem just an observation. So now I have the perfect lime or lemon pie filling to take to potlucks. I can't wait to try banana.

I had made Almond Impossible pie but I thought it was too eggy tasting. Lemon seemed like a good way to minimize the egg taste. I made some changes: I used 2 whole eggs & 4 whites + 2 tsp. melted sweet butter. 1/2 c. Meyer lemon juice and 1/4 c. Lemon juice. I added 2 tsps. Meyer lemon zest. It's good...I served it with raspberry coulis & cool whip since the dinner I made it for had been cancelled & I didn't want to whip the cream for my husband & myself. I think the recipe still needs some tweaking - less coconut perhaps, maybe 1/8 tsp. salt added. I liked that it wasn't super sweet. I think I'll also add 1/2 tsp pure lemon extract next time to amp up the citrus taste. It is quick & a recipe well worth tinkering with to perfection.

I was a little hesitant to make this after reading previous reviews but I am so glad I did. 
I did use a half cup of lemon juice and added the rind, I also used 3 eggs instead of 4. 
This turned out amazing, we wanted to eat the whole pan! Lemon and coconut are delicious together and this is a really quick, easy and yummy summer dessert. It would also be good with whipped cream on top!
